summary: The observed llama.cpp Ouro port is an open, unmerged upstream PR. Its submitted graph aliases physical weights across recurrent logical layers, applies branch and inter-loop norms, uses logical-layer KV indices, and exposes graph callbacks. These artifacts contradict any assertion that only Proxima can express Ouro recurrence. The inspected patch has no LoopCD operation or separate recurrent-state consumer API; this is a bounded source inventory.

The native Ouro research example reads official BF16 safetensors, binds its recurrent graph using existing tensor operations, retains first/final readouts and applies fixed LoopCD. The regular architecture registry has no Ouro registration. General chat/generation integration requires an architecture adapter, tokenizer/template compatibility and loop/layer-separated incremental KV handling. Prototype execution is distinct from that integration. Relative setup effort, matched llama.cpp latency/CoV and quality comparisons are unmeasured.

Ouro embeds the token prefix, transforms the current hidden tensor through the shared layer stack, applies loop normalization, and feeds that updated tensor into the next pass. The same learned transformation receives a different hidden tensor each pass. Refinement denotes this internal transformation; quality improvement for an individual pass is not guaranteed by the computation. LoopCD is a separate readout contrast using first/final predictions from the same prefix.

metric: candidate logits before and after fixed recurrent-depth contrast
corpus: pinned ByteDance/Ouro-1.4B; prefix IDs [19556,905,30], decoded bytes Hello world.
